title: CmdPal: window briefly resizes when shown on a monitor with different DPI

judgment.rationale: The mixed-DPI summon sequence is explicit, a maintainer already identified asynchronous settling as a possibility, and a November 15 follow-up says the glitch persists.
evidence: The original report uses PowerToys 0.98 dev build and two monitors with different DPI settings.
Maintainer jiripolasek says positioning already occurs while cloaked; waiting for settling might cost 200–300 ms and icon refresh may compete on the UI thread.
A later commenter reports continued occurrence: https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/issues/45957#issuecomment-6889104063

Current main MainWindow.xaml.cs: ShowHwndCore invokes positionWindow, shows the HWND, then calls Uncloak without an explicit layout-settled barrier; MoveAndResizeDpiAware suppresses default DPI resizing during the move.
Related #46289 covers a similar cross-monitor glitch; issue-number PR search found no direct implementation. The prior artifact's empty assignee assertion is unsupported and is not retained.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce on mixed-DPI monitors and measure layout completion versus uncloaking before considering a bounded first-frame readiness change.

proposed_fixes.title: Gate mixed-DPI reveal on target layout readiness
proposed_fixes.root_cause: DPI-triggered layout or icon work may not settle before Uncloak, although bounds are moved while hidden; this is not yet a measured causal ordering.
plan: Measure the DPI/layout/paint sequence around positionWindow and Uncloak on the public repro.
If confirmed, defer reveal until target-size layout is ready using a bounded completion condition rather than an unconditional 300-ms delay.
Keep same-DPI warm activation fast and add mixed-DPI reveal regression coverage.
verification: Check first-frame bounds at 100%/150% and 100%/200%, both directions, without adding fixed warm-show delay.

confidence.rationale: The report, maintainer explanation and reveal ordering agree on the investigation boundary; no first-frame trace proves the root cause.

reproduce.title: Verify reported Command Palette behavior
reproduce.version_requirement: 0.98 dev build from report; verify 0.102/current main
prerequisites: Two monitors with different scaling factors; Command Palette configured to appear on the active monitor.
steps: Configure two displays at different DPI scales and leave Command Palette cloaked on one.
Move focus to the other monitor and summon Command Palette with its hotkey.
Capture the first visible frame and repeat in both directions, warm and cold, with icon-heavy results.
reproduce.expected_result: The first visible frame has the final size and scale without a visible post-show resize.
